note: The two sets are essentially identical: all 19 claims match in entity, attribute, value, unit and quote, with the sole difference that Set B adds the condition "load of laundry" to the clothes-drying eligibility claim. Both sets correctly bind the dishwasher temperatures (120 °F full points, 115 °F half points), the 8-place-setting capacity, the two-sensor redundancy, the disabled heated-drying option, and the Clothes Dryer Subcontest weight thresholds (≤100 / 100–110 / ≥110 % of original weight), with quotes that support them. Both sets also repeat the same facts under two names (sensor count, wash/rinse cycles, 120 °F, 115 °F, and the three scoring bands stated both under "Clothes Dryer Subcontest" and "clothes-drying task"), and both omit the same facts (temperature-of-record rule, cycle-completion signal, cycle-interruption definition, load state allowance, two-loads-per-day rule). The single added condition in B is too marginal to make the sets meaningfully different.
remarks: Both sets double-state several facts (2 sensors, 1 wash/rinse cycle, 120 °F, 115 °F, and each of the three clothes-drying scoring bands under both "Clothes Dryer Subcontest" and "clothes-drying task"), inflating the count without adding information. Shared omissions worth adding: the higher-of-two-sensor-readings temperature-of-record rule (with the defective-sensor exception), cycle completion confirmed by audible/visible signal, the definition of cycle "interruption", the allowance to run the dishwasher empty/partially/fully loaded and soiled or clean, the two-loads-per-day requirement with separately scored loads, and the requirement to demonstrate towel-visible drying methods to the architecture and market appeal juries.
